# MMF demand, bill holdings and G10 bill markets: detail

Companion to `SKILL.md` sections 5 and 9. Figures are as printed in the cited notes; units are $bn unless stated.
Chart-read levels are approximate and are labelled so.

## 1. MMF AUM growth vs the 3m bill yield

Average year-on-year MMF AUM growth by 3m bill yield bucket (BofA, Jul 2025; BofA, Oct 2025):

| 3m bill yield | AUM growth, Jul 2025 note | AUM growth, Oct 2025 note |
|---|---|---|
| 0% | 1.83% | 1.83% |
| 1% | -0.20% | -0.20% |
| 2% | 13.66% | 13.66% |
| 3% | 9.77% | 9.77% |
| 3.5% | 11.67% | 11.67% |
| 4% | 13.78% | 13.89% |
| 5% | 17.48% | 17.48% |
| 6% | 15.70% | 15.70% |

The 4% value differs between the two notes (13.78% vs 13.89%), which is a vintage difference. Rule of thumb: flat at
0-1%, about 10% a year at 2-3%, about 15% a year at 4-6%. AUM is correlated with front-end yields with a lag (the
table uses one-year-ahead growth). At a 3.5% terminal rate, BofA said AUM could still grow more than 10% a year
(BofA, Jul 2025).

MMF balances (about $7tn) have fallen only twice in 30 years (2003-05 and after the GFC). Barclays does not expect
rate cuts to pull money out, because MMF yields stay above deposit rates while deposit rates fall faster
(Barclays, Jan 2025). MMFs did not see outflows from rate cuts "not even 50bp". Historically, outflows need rates
below about 2% (Conks, Sep 2024).

## 2. Demand build-up (BofA, Oct 2025)

- MMF AUM $7.34tn x 10% growth = $734bn of new AUM.
- x bill allocation about 33% = about $242bn. The note prints about $225bn, which implies a bill allocation of
  about 30.6%. Use 30-33% and show the range.
- Other demand (rest of world and other investors) grew about 10% a year post-COVID, +$350bn. Haircut to
  $150-250bn a year as reliable.
- Total demand: $375-475bn a year. FY26 supply: about $600bn. FY27: $1.1tn or more.
- Gap: at least $125bn in FY26 and up to $725bn in FY27.
- Fed bill-buying channels in that note: MBS-to-bill reinvestment $120-240bn a year (immediately after QT); liability
  growth (currency, reserves, TGA) about $200bn a year, possibly lagged; reserve backfill about $150bn, less certain.
  Total about $300-450bn a year.

## 3. Holders of bills (Z.1, Q2 2025, bills held by the public $5.78tn; BofA, Oct 2025)

| Holder | $bn | Share |
|---|---|---|
| MMFs | 1,918 | 33.2% |
| Rest of world (official 402, private 1,013) | 1,415 | 24.5% |
| Insurers and pensions | 409 | 7.1% |
| Depository institutions | 419 | 7.2% |
| Fed | 194 | 3.35% |
| Other financial | 385 | |
| Non-financial business | 49 | |

The residual of about $0.8-1tn is most likely households. MMF share of bills outstanding (ex Fed): 30-40% (BofA,
Oct 2026); about 38% at about $2.8tn with government MMFs holding about half their assets in USTs (Barclays, Oct 2026).

Bills outstanding vs MMF bill holdings (BofA, Jul 2025): June 2025 5,784 vs 1,914 = 33% (the low); January 2025 6,380
vs 2,531 = 40%; November 2024 6,390 vs 2,570 = 40%.

Government MMF snapshot, June 2025 (BofA, Jul 2025): Treasury debt 2,437 (-28 on the month), Treasury repo 1,623
(+97), agency debt 885 (+1), agency repo 756 (+24), total 5,877 (+104; +897 year on year). Prime 1,180. AUM about
+13% year on year. Seven-day yields 3.97% government vs 4.04% prime. ON RRP MMF take-up was $390bn at June quarter-end
(about 85% of the total). MMFs cut bills in June ahead of the 4 July resolution.

MMF WAM and WLA (BofA, Jul 2025): government MMF WAM about 40 days, near historical highs, so there is little room to
extend into bills beyond about 1.5 months. Prime WAM was about 3 days longer quarter-to-date. Prime WLA was above its
50% minimum threshold.

Regulatory WAM limit: under 60 days. Overnight repo counts as zero-day maturity and gives daily liquidity, which
is why MMFs hold 1m bills and overnight repo (Conks, Jan 2025; Conks, Jun 2023). Rule 2a-7 maximum maturity is 397
days.

CP: MMFs hold about 20% of CP (BofA, Jul 2025); the CP market is up to 270 days, mostly under three months.
Regulatory constraints have made MMFs a declining share of CP investors (BofA, Jul 2025).

## 4. Bill share governance

| Source | Level | Context |
|---|---|---|
| TBAC (as cited) | 15% lower bound; about 20% target over time | Aug 2023 guidance: comfortable in the range of the longer-term historical share of 22.4% for some time |
| BofA (Nov 2024) | 22.5% rough upper tolerance; prior tolerance 22.5% of marketable debt; new tolerance up to 25% (+1 standard deviation since 2000) | Assume bill growth until rates decline or the share hits +1 sd |
| Conks (Jul 2025) | Up to 25% barely raises rollover risk; 30% or more "is pushing it" | Bill share as a term-out trigger |
| Citi (Aug 2026) | About 27% with coupon increases delayed to Feb 2028; about 29% by end-2028 with no coupon increases | CY2026 funding need 2,127, bill share 23.1%; CY2027 2,323, 24.5% |

Trigger to term out (BofA, Jul 2025): long-end nominal yields below 3% and real yields below 50bp. In 2021-22 the
average 10y, 20y and 30y nominal yields were 2.19%, 2.63% and 2.58%, with real yields of -0.26%, 0.22% and 0.27%.

The late-October 2025 curve was inverted from 1m to 1y (Conks, Oct 2025). By May 2026 it had un-inverted. Bills
outstanding chart labels look mis-scaled against the total, so treat them with care.

## 6. Money-market rate corridor, 1 July 2025 snapshot (BofA, Jul 2025)

Discount window and SRF 4.50; IORB 4.40; EFFR and OBFR 4.33; SOFR 4.30; ON RRP 4.25 (the floor). Tri-party Treasury
4.39; 1m bill 4.22; overnight FHLB discount notes 4.16. So the 1m bill traded below ON RRP. Ceilings and floors hold
"in theory (not always in practice)" (Conks, Oct 2024).

Rates hierarchy in normal times (Conks, Oct 2024), high to low: FIMA repo (public offshore ceiling); swap line at OIS
+25bp (private offshore ceiling); FX-swap implied USD rate; SRF rate (ceiling for SOFR, GCF, tri-party); discount rate
(ceiling for EFFR); IORB, EFFR, GCF, SOFR, tri-party; foreign repo pool (public floor); ON RRP (private floor); repo
specials below the floor.

## 7. Fed bill purchases (RMOs) and the balance sheet

- Realised RMOs: about $38bn in December 2025, $48bn in January, $54bn in February, $60bn in March (the peak) and $47bn
  in April 2026 (Conks, May 2026).
- Projected: about $40bn a month in May-June 2026, then about $35bn a month July-December, including about $15bn of MBS
  reinvested into bills. Cumulative purchases about $550bn by December 2026 (Conks, May 2026).
- Bills held by the Fed above $1tn by early 2027 (Conks, Mar 2026).
- Treasury cash-management buybacks and Fed RMOs each took about $200bn of bills out of the market by April 2026
  (Conks, Apr 2026).
- SOMA WAM 8.70 years (March 2026) and 8.45 years (May 2026); the Treasury-market WAM is about 71 months (Conks, May 2026).
- Stablecoins: net positive for bills, adding a bid for T-bills and reducing the need for RMOs, because banks pay for
  physical currency with reserves (Conks, Mar 2026).

## 8. Non-USD bill markets

**JPY.** T-bills are FB and TB, with 3, 6 and 12-month tenors and 3m weekly auctions. Overseas investors held about 67%
of T-bills at end-2022, against 6% of JGBs excluding bills (BofA, Apr 2023), because lending USD to Japanese banks via
the basis earns the US-Japan spread plus a premium. FY2023 T-bill issuance was 50.7tn yen, down 13.9tn on FY2022.

3m T-bill ASW fair value (J.P. Morgan, Feb 2025): a regression on the 3m USD/JPY cross-currency basis, monthly T-bill net
issuance and the 3m GC/OIS spread, rolling over 12 months. The February 2025 residual was about -4bp (bills rich vs
fair). Inelastic demand for collateral posted to foreign central banks keeps bills rich vs fair value.

3m JGB$ASW decomposition (J.P. Morgan, Jun 2025): (a) 3m CP minus 3m bill (credit and stress) + (b) regulatory and
liquidity costs + (c) year-end turn premium of about +15bp in October-December. June 2025: (a) 9.5bp + (b) 9.2bp = 18.7bp
model vs 17.9bp actual. September 2024: (a) 10.6bp + (b) 15.0bp, with a model of 26.7bp vs 13.2bp actual, which the
note calls broadly consistent.

Money-market fund behaviour in Japan: Money Reserve Funds (MRFs) hold a WAM of about 21.8 days, steady over the past
year, and buy T-bills on cheapness vs OIS; they do not chase richness (J.P. Morgan, Feb 2025). MRF T-bill holdings
moved from 743bn yen (October 2024) to 655 (November), 672 (December) and 1,000 (January 2025), with repo falling in
the same window (J.P. Morgan, Feb 2025). The BoJ "other deposits" line, remunerated at the Tokyo repo rate less 5bp,
mirrors foreign bill demand (BofA, Apr 2023; J.P. Morgan, Feb 2025).

Japan-specific calendar: the 1 April turn. Strip the year-end and 1 April turn before reading policy from money-market
rates (Duering, 2021).

**EUR.** USD lenders park cash in French and other euro bills. Euro ASWs cheapened and bills underperformed OIS, easing
the collateral shortage (Citi, Dec 2024). Deposit facility rate caps GC, most visibly in Bunds, and becomes the MRO
if banks are balance-sheet constrained (Citi, Dec 2024). In October 2026 OAT stress moved to the front end, with French
bills cheap vs ESTR and Schatz-ESTR and FRA-ESTR wider (Barclays, Oct 2026). Under the PEPP (March 2020) the minimum
maturity of 28 days allowed German bills to be bought (Tuckman and Serrat, 2022).

CME EUR/USD 3m cross-currency basis futures traded about -2.5 to -7bp in 2025, crossed zero in December 2025 and peaked
near +3bp in January 2026 (Conks, Oct 2025; Conks, Mar 2026).

**AUD.** BBSW-OIS normalised to about 8.5bp from the wides (Citi STIRT, Aug 2026). TN -15bp AONIA-SOFR in August 2026.
AUD FRA-OIS looks too narrow vs the hedged cost of bank offshore issuance (J.P. Morgan, Jun 2025).

**NZD.** Tax outflows cut settlement cash from 26.5bn to 24bn. NZIONA-SOFR 1w to 1m tightened 5-7.5bp in August 2026
while forward-forward spreads were stable (Citi STIRT, Aug 2026).

**GBP.** Bank of England reserves stabilising at 385-530bn set the cap on balance-sheet-driven basis moves (J.P. Morgan,
Jun 2025). Buyback news confirmed reliance on short-end issuance, reflexively met by more bills, removing USD from the
front end at the margin (Citi STIRT, Aug 2026, GBP desk view of US buybacks).

**CAD, CHF, SEK, NOK.** The research base for this skill has no bill-specific material for these markets. Use the
local auction and day-count conventions from `fi-g10-market-conventions`. Canadian bill YTM definitions differ above and
below one year (Darbyshire, undated).

**Corridor floor and ceiling tools by central bank (BofA, Jul 2025):** Fed IORB and ON RRP (floor); SRF and discount
window (ceiling). ECB deposit facility (floor) and MRO (ceiling). BoE standing repo and discount window (ceiling). BoC
deposit rate (bottom of range) and standing facility (top). RBA exchange settlement balances at cash rate less 10bp
(floor) and overnight facility at target plus 25bp (ceiling). BoJ complementary deposit facility (floor) and
complementary lending facility (ceiling).

## 9. Chart-read caveats
- Levels read from charts (bill curves, bills outstanding, MMF holdings) are approximations. Verify against `auctions`
  and `bond_quotes` before use.
- The 2019 Exhibit 5 peak value conflicts with its own stated sign in one source; drop it or flag it.
- Bills outstanding labels in some Conks charts look mis-scaled against total bills.
